text:
Nick Caserio reviews C.J. Stroud and Nico Collins performance on Texans All-Access
Executive vice president and general manager Nick Caserio discussed the performances of quarterback C.J. Stroud and wide receiver Nico Collins during an appearance with Marc Vandermeer and John Harris, according to a Sep. 16 conversation on Texans All-Access.
Caserio said of Stroud, "Did a nice job, made good decisions with the football, distributed to multiple players. There were 10 or 11 skilled players that touched the ball. So a lot of this is just throwing the ball to the open receiver and understanding what they're doing defensively." He highlighted Stroud's ability in the pocket, referencing one play where Stroud scrambled on third-and-long for a significant gain: "He did a good job of kind of maneuvering within the pocket a little bit. And he had to scramble on third-and-long where they ended up playing man coverage where they didn't account for the quarterback, and he was able to turn that into a chunk play opportunity." Caserio concluded his assessment by saying, "Overall, did a lot of good things. Pretty solid."
Turning attention to Collins, Caserio said his strong performances have become expected: "You almost assume that that's what you're going to get on a weekly basis," he said. "He's just such a unique player. Does a lot of things well." Caserio described one particular play early in the game: "Even the hitch that he caught there early in the game — it was a catch-and-run, he turned a five-yard completion into a 12- to 13-yard gain... It's a simple play, but it becomes a quasi-explosive play because of his ability to catch and run."
Caserio also noted Collins' ability in contested situations: "Made multiple contested catches," he said. "There were multiple plays where the defender was draped on him, but he's just so big and strong, has good hands, and that's kind of who he is." He credited Stroud for setting up another key moment: "Made the play down the field there on the sideline — the third down was a really great throw by C.J."
Looking ahead at team needs for success this season, Caserio stated, "We're going to need him [Collins], and we're going to need all of our skilled players throughout the course of this season."
